column3: The Hebrew says the people traveled “by the hand of Moses and Aaron”; BSB says “under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.”
The Hebrew says “by the mouth of the LORD”; BSB uses “At the LORD’s command.”

The Hebrew repeats “the first month” and uses the images “with a raised hand” and “before the eyes of all Egypt”; BSB states the month once and says “defiantly” and “in full view of all the Egyptians.”
The Hebrew has plural “judgments” against Egypt’s gods; BSB uses singular “judgment.”
The Hebrew changes from plural setting out to singular turning and then plural camping; BSB uses plural subjects throughout.
The Hebrew names Elim twice; BSB gives the name once and uses “where” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew names the sea with the reed word, “Sea of Reeds”; BSB uses “Red Sea.”
